name: Homefries
desc: Homefries is a great warm-up problem but hardly the give-me V0 you might expect. Stand start and climb right side of steep slab face starting just left of the tree with incut jug behind tree for right hand. Go up and move left to finish up the center on increasing slabby/slopey terrain
location: Large boulder on Right as you enter the Colflesh area. Same finish as Ham (V1). Starts to the right of Ham. Bacon (V1) starts and finishes left of ham. Right side of face.
protection: Bouldering Pad: Nice landing, one pad will do.

photos.cap: The finish for both homefries and ham

name: Bacon
desc: Stand start and climb left side of steep slabby face to good holds and left exit.
location: Large boulder on Right as you enter the Colflesh area. Start and finish left of Ham (V1), which is left of homefries. Left line up face.

name: Pancakes
desc: Great moves on positive holds. Start on side-pull and stand up to large horizontal then move to nice finger jam in crack and crank up onto better holds above. Finish on easy slab.
location: Left side (downhill side) of Homefries boulder just left of blunt arête.
protection: Bouldering Pad: Good landing but don’t miss the pad or you could take a tumble.

photos.cap: Paula moving from the start crimp to the jug on Pancakes v0

name: Scrapple
desc: Climb this little guy for a quickie ride on a surprisingly fun V0. Sit start on obvious holds then move to lip and jugs above. Setup for a high step and finish.
location: Off by itself ten feet right of the Homefries boulder.

name: BG Warmup
desc: Stand start.Start matched at the top of the left arete and traverse right across the top of the boulder until you reach a good sidepull on the right side of the boulder and top out.
location: On the short boulder between the boulder Scrapple is on and the boulder where the majority of the Breakfast boulder routes are.

name: Ham
desc: Another great warm-up between Homefries (V0) and Bacon (V1). Stand start and climb center of steep slab face straight up to top.
location: Large boulder on Right as you enter the Colflesh area. Same finish as Homefires (V0). But homefries starts right of ham. And Bacon (V1) starts and finishes left of ham. Center line up face.
protection: Bouldering Pad: One pad, flat landing.

photos.cap: Ryan Salkeld crimping the puzzling start of Ham (V0).  Bacon (V0) and Homefries  (V0) also pictured. Photo by Greg Sudlow.
The finish of both ham and homefries
Tim Armstrong heading up this awkward line

name: Gumdrops
desc: Short problem on dirty face. Move up on good edges to top, mantel and finish.
location: Small boulder just right of Colflesh boulder. Problem starts beside fallen tree.
protection: Bouldering pad: Landing is sloped so two pads are preferable.

name: Green Eggs
desc: Gird your loins for this one! A fall at the top is definitely a bad idea. Start on easy holds to fun mantel then reach for sloppy rail high above. Man up (or woman up) and smear blank face to reach jug at top.
location: Left around the backside of the Homefries boulder (boulder on right when entering area).
protection: Bouldering pad: Bring a pad but there really is no way to protect the top so climb strong! And maybe, only do this problem once just to say you did it.

photos.cap: Green Eggs (V1). Photo by Greg Sudlow.

name: Path Less Traveled
desc: Work your way up the slab with long moves between good holds
location: Around the corner to the right of Torretti.

name: New Kid On The Bloc
desc:
Stand start.
Start matched on a prominent jug with a good foot out right. Work yourself up over a slopey finish.
location: The short boulder just left of the main Colflesh boulder. Prominent start hold is just left of the arete closest to the boulder.

name: Velveteen Rabbit
desc: Stand start.Start with a left hand sidepull and right hand high slopey crimp. Make a big move straight up to a jug and top out.
location: Boulder to the right of Gumdrop.

name: Oh Shit
desc: Sit start matched on large triangle sidepull (same as Poison Ivy). Go left to a two finger edge, then a sloper. Move out left to crimp in middle of the scoop, then top out thru the scoop.
location: Large scoop on left side of Colflesh boulder (large boulder left and downhill from area’s entrance).
protection: Bouldering pad: Take two pads or a spotter. Landing is good but sloped downhill.

photos.cap: Ryan Salkeld moving out to crimp in middle of scoop. Oh Shit (V0). Photo by Greg Sudlow.

name: Gumdrops
desc: Squat start.Start low with hands on the prominent crack and great feet. Move right hand up to the arete and work your way up left to a slopey, crimpy top out.
location: Boulder just to the right of the Colflesh Boulder. This route is opposite Path Less Traveled.

name: Poison Ivy
desc: Great sustained bouldering on long traverse. Good footwork required. Sit start matched on large triangle sidepull (same as Oh Shit), then traverse right and up diagonal crack to nose. Top out the same as Coleflesh, straight up on good holds and easy slab.
location: Obvious diagonal crack finishing above Colflesh problem (V5).
protection: Bouldering pad: Take two pads or an attentive spotter to protect the traverse. Landing is good all the way.

photos.cap: Tim Armstrong chalking up before heading into the crux
Jodie on the Poison Ivy traverse
Greg Sudlow on the Posion Ivy traverse (V0). Photo by Ryan Salkeld.

name: Jenn Savage
desc: Start on head high crimps and bad right foot smear, crank to positive edge then move up to lip and easy slab above.
location: Center face of large boulder left and slightly downhill from access trail entrance.

photos.cap: Greg Sudlow reaching the lip on Jenn Savage (V2). Photo by Ryan Salkeld.

name: Torretti
desc: Start on head high sloper and low side pull. Move left to positive edge before pulling lip and finish.
location: Far right of Colflesh bolder intersecting with Jenn Savage midway up.
protection: Good landing. One well placed pad will do.

name: Malcolm X
desc: Starts to the left of Colflesh, climbs straight up the face to about 16 ft.
location: Colflesh area

name: Colflesh Direct
fa: Joel Terretti or Chet Gross? Late 1990s
desc: The obvious hard line up the center of the Colflesh boulder, left of Jenn Savage.

photos.cap: Elan on crimp match. Hard part is hitting it and bringing the feet up to deadpoint the jug.

name: Colflesh X
desc: A low start to Colflesh that starts on the crimp to the left which is the start of Malcolm X. From the crimp, go right into the start of Colflesh. Adds a few weird fun moves and mixes up the sequence a bit.
location: On the Coleflesh boulder.

name: Wholesome
desc: Start right, traverse left to bulge, top out
location: Small boulder just downhill from body snap

name: Energy
desc: Sit start low then climb little arête and move right at top to finish out on easy slab.
location: Uphill edge of the Body Snap boulder (large boulder at the bottom of the area). Just right of Body Snap (V4/V6).
protection: Bouldering Pad: Bring two pads to protect against the jumble of small rocks surrounding the start.

name: Havit
desc: This problem may be over in just a few moves but figuring out how to get into sequence can take some time. Stand and match on good edge then move up to top of shallow scoop. Pull through and finish.
location: Downhill face of Body Snap boulder, the large boulder at the bottom of Colflesh area.
protection: Bouldering Pad: Good landing, one pad.

name: Fiction
desc:
Hanging start, top out. 
Start at the lowest point of the prominent ledge and work your way up and left to the crack system. Move up through the cracks to a slopey top out.
location: Around the arete left of Body Snap. The prominent start ledge will indicate the route.

name: Lucky Charms
desc: Sit down start w/ LH on a small crimp and RH on a nice pinch. Work your way up (jugs) and around the boulder. If you top out early, it's more V1. If you go around, it's more V2.
location: On the way to the Body Snap boulder from the Breakfast boulders, there's a small boulder that juts out from the ground to your right. This is your lucky charm.

name: Body Snap
desc: Start on the prow of the boulder around the corner from Colflesh boulder. You'll walk across a log to get there.Start with a decent right hand and a low left hand crimp, make the first move to the pinch and move to the right hand out to an edge, from there work up to the top out.

photos.cap: Sunni (Left) and Zach (Right). Zach has his right hand on the starting hold. Hop up to stick a good left, choose your smears/foot-crystals and power to the sloping corner. Finish with the variety of holds and feet.

name: Faction
desc: Crux is at the beginning. This problem starts below fiction, with a decent crimp ledge a few feet off the ground. The easiest way, and possibly the only way, of climbing this route is with a feet-first toe hook start in the first hold of fiction, then pulling into that hold with your body almost upside down. The separated rock under the body snap boulder is off, and you can top out anywhere you want within the fiction area.(In my send, I had to push off the ground with my left arm and kick my right toe into the wall to assist my left foot getting to the bat-hang position.)
location: On the body snap boulder just to the right of fiction, start with your hands in the long crimp edge above the small rock underneath the bodysnap boulder.

photos.cap: Fiction left, Faction center, Body Snap Right

name: "15 Project"
desc: Thin holds to slopers at the lip. Exit via an engaging mantle.
location: Located right of Body Snap (sit) and left of Energy.

photos.cap: "15 Project" in Colflesh Area of Mt. Gretna

name: Body Snap Sit
desc:
An area classic, one of the most tried in all of Gretna! 
 Sit start with a good undercling and a crimp. Pull up and snag the side pull, pick some feet and make crux long move out left to good crimps. Follow the crimps left up to a big sloper. Then make a tension move to the lip to a causal topout. 
 Although this is called Body Snap Sit the only move it shares with Body Snap is the top out.
location: Obvious low starting holds on the Body Snap Boulder.

photos.cap: John catching the hold on Body Snap Sit v6
John goin' for the slopey hold on Body Snap Sit v6
Opening move on the sit, foot not on the block. Sunkook boutta go for it

name: Sur La Pointe
desc:
Sur La Pointe is a Joel classic. He was all about this problem at the time and it has a very nice name (look up the definition). This is a challenging and tricky one move wonder dyno from a perfect one pad edge that accommodates eight fingers. The right toe frontpoints in a small, shallow pocket, smear the left foot and launch for the sloping lip! 
 Surprised you only gained a few vertical feet? It is difficult to generate any pull with the hands at all, everything is about leaping with the right toe pocket. It very much helps if you have a new edge on your shoes. I tried this probably 50 times before succeeding.
location: On a boulder downhill from the Colflesh area proper. The climb will be facing downhill away from you and would be challenging to find without a local.

name: Intro Slab Left
desc: Stand start.Start on the big ledge and smear up to the top out.
location: On a boulder right of the main Nector boulder. The problem is on the left side of the boulder.

name: Intro Slab Right
desc: Stand start.Start with hands on a long crimp and move up through good crimps to the top out.
location: On a boulder right of the main Nector boulder. The problem is on the right side of the boulder.

name: Nectar Vector
desc: Sit start at arete and follow obvious edges and jugs to top. Fun.
location: Downhill from Colflesh Boulder. Left most line on Nectar Boulder.

name: April Showers
desc: Start on jug, go up slopers and mantle directly up. There's a left variation that's a bit harder.
location: First boulder you pass when you go down the path from Coleflesh/Colflesh to the Nectar boulder.
protection: 1 pad should be OK, two wouldn't hurt.

name: Sweet Nector
desc: Stand Start with your left hand in a high "pocket" (where two seems create a small gap) and right hand on a crimp. Gain high right foot and grab far right undercling. Top out on slopers. The top is a wrestling match but there's probably some good foot beta that will make this part easier.
location: On the face of the nectar boulder, just right of Nector Vector.
protection: Two pads and a spotter will be good. Lots of bumps to cover at the base.

photos.cap: Climb face left of arete, topping out on slopers and a right hand sidepull (sidepull better used as a sloper w/ thumb).

name: Wrinkles and Toenails
desc: Stand start.Follow the vertical crack to an easy top out.
location: On the boulder to the right of the main Elephant Boulder. This route is on the far right side.

name: That
desc: Stand start.Start with a good right hand sidepull in the crack with your left hand on the lower left flake for support. Using high feet, work your way up over the top.
location: This boulder is just downhill of the main Elephant Boulder. This problem is on the left side of the boulder as you’re walking down from the Elephant Boulder and climber’s right of This.

name: Elephant Walk
desc:
Stand start. 
Start by leaning into the wall and smearing your hands. Smear your way up through crimps to the top out. An even easier variation of this goes up the crack to the right of this.
location: Just right of the arete of the Elephant Boulder.

name: Inner Light
desc: Start at the base of the obvious vertical crack on the left side of the boulder with a pocket and rounded edge. Climb straight up on decent hands and small feet using the crack for both where necessary.
location: Left side of the main elephant boulder starting at the base of the obvious vertical crack.

name: Outer Dark
desc: Stand start compressing the "trunk" feature immediately right of the "inner light" start. Climb right with great feet to follow a diagonal crack with some of the best holds at Gretna. Turn right around the corner with some smearing to stand up and top out the tall slab.
location: Start is immediately right of "inner light" on the left side of the main elephant boulder.

name: Banjo Walk
desc: Obvious good foot shelf to start, then head up to small holds with one scary feeling high step before you top out.
location: Just left of Wrinkles & Toenails

name: Balance Issues
desc: Start foot in crack and use crack under-cling. Balance to shallow crimp and top out right. Short but fun.
location: Start in diagonal crack to the left of Outer Dark and Inner Light at Elephant Boulder.

photos.cap: View of the problem around the corner from Inner Light

name: The Other Thing
desc: Sit start.Start with a good left hand sidepull and right hand on the arete. Move up using the arete on the right and various left hand holds to the top out.
location: On the downhill face of the boulder just below the boulder with the This and That problems.

name: This
desc: Stand start.Start with a high left crimp and a high right sloper using a good ledge as a foot. Make a move for the top and flop your way over the top.
location: This boulder is just downhill of the main Elephant Boulder. This problem is on the downhill face.

name: The Balance of Darkness and Light
desc: Start as for balance issues, instead of topping out trend right into outer darkness and then into inner light and top out
location: Start as for balance issues

name: Excavator
desc: Sit start w/ a horizontal LH crimp and a RH sidepull crimp. Work your way up to a nice RH sloper pinch and then up.
location: Same boulder as "this" or "that", below the Elephant Boulder.

name: Corner Crack
desc: The corner crack to the left of Islander. Climb up the crack.
location: The corner crack to the left of Islander.

name: Tackle Box
desc: Follow large crack traversing left a few moves before moving up on large holds to top. A good cool down or part of an endurance circuit with other area problems.
location: Left side of large boulder. Obvious hand crack you come to when first entering the Prow area.

photos.cap: Sinking a jam high up on this classic!

name: Vigilante Direct
desc: Start as for Vigilante which some call the Warm Up Crack. Get off the ground and where the crack turns left head straight up and onto the slab above. The holds are not obvious from the ground and will most likely have no chalk but they will appear upon closer inspection.
location: Front side of Warm Up boulder in the Prow Area. Begins on obvious crack.

photos.cap: Zach France climbing Vigilante Direct in sub freezing temperatures.

name: Vigilante (aka Warm-up Crack)
desc: Start with hands high in crack and step up. Follow crack as it tends left and finish on good holds and slab.
location: Front side (downhill facing) of large boulder you come to when entering the Prow area. Ten feet right of Tackle Box.
protection: A few pads to protect traverse or an attentive spotter.

photos.cap: In the guide book they give this V2 and call it something else. V1 is probably more accurate for Gretna grades. Really fun climb. The top part is a bit tricky. [[106748981]]
Zach France on a below freezing ascent of the Warm Up Crack

name: Chet's Children
desc: Stand start and climb face to good hold at top.
location: Face left of large Tackle Box crack.

name: The Force
desc: Grab the obvious jugs in the crack pull up for a good crimp and grab the undercling in the crack. Reach up high for the top then go left for the top out.
location: Left of Darkstar left of the big tree

photos.cap: A view of Lenny pulling off the start of the boulder. [[109687698]]

name: Vee 3
desc: Start on the obvious jug and topout at the highest point to the left.

name: Astroboy
desc: No beta spray here. Just a big offwidth/ squeeze chimney on clean rock that beckons to be climbed. Stand start on the microwave sized blocs in the back of the crack. Traverse out the crack to the jug and pull the lip.
location: Immediately right of the PROW. Stand start on the two blocks in the back of the offwidth.

photos.cap:
Dave G in Astroboy
Photo taken by Lily Cerritos
Gus just starting Astroboy. Photo by Andrew Burr.
Seth about midway through the offwidth/chimney portion. Photo by Andrew Burr.

name: Dark Side aka Teachers Pet
desc: Squat start with good holds and a decent chip for your left foot and big rail for right. Pull up to a gaston grab a crimp and reach for the top.
location: On the opposite back side of Serenity Crack under a tree in a small corridor

photos.cap: Out of the light and into the dark
Moving from the roof on IT
Pic of that sweet sweet heel hook.

name: Cousin IT
desc: same start hold as IT, reach out right to crack. work your way out the crack to the lip. mantel on the lip and top out. keep feet to the left on IT. **right wall is off**.

name: Brain Wave
desc: Stand start with a left hand crimp and right hand in a slopey seam. Ride the lip moving left until you hit the highest point of the boulder.
location: Behind Islander. Go around the back where you would downclimb for Islander and this climb will be right in front of you.

name: Phase One
desc: Sit start on a jug to the far left of the boulder. Use a toe or heel to move out right on slopers and small edges to a jug. Top out on the far right side.
location: Off the trail on the left

name: Islander
desc: Definitely worth a mention in any conversation debating the best route at Gretna, and could stack up against any area classic anywhere. Both the sit (V8) and the stand (V7) are amazing. The sit used to be V9 but a hold broke and brought it down a grade. No matter how you start it the top is tricky and there are a few different ways to do it. Whether you go with a heel hook, match, or all out dyno is up to you. No matter what you chose you'll be happy you stuck it.
location: On the Prow Boulder. Islander and The Prow share the same start. Stay on the face for Islander, bust right around the arete for The Prow. Do them both, they're rad!
protection: a few pads. It's not a high ball but it's high enough and there's some spice at the top. The landing area is nice and flat.

photos.cap: DD sending The Islander (V8) at Mt. Gretna, PA. November 2016. danallardphoto.com
Sticking the crux 2 and 3 finger match

name: Testicules
desc:
Testicules climbs the blunt right arete on the main face of the Warm Up boulder of the Prow area. Begin by pulling onto a large foot with a small left crimp and the right hand squeezing nothing around the blunt corner. A right heel in this same blank, chalky spot will allow both hands to move into a crimpy seam around the left side of the feature. Delicately transition to slopers at the lip, then snag the incut hold. Pull onto the slab and topout. You may want to scope the topout slab before trying. A cold weather problem.
Testicules is a Gretna classic with great movement. It can be frustrating until one figures out the subtleties. I believe that name may stem from a combination of testicles and Hercules.
location: Blunt right arete on the main face of the Warm Up boulder.
protection: Pads and a spotter. There is a rock around the right that I've landed on precariously before.

photos.cap: Matthew Bashista sending Testicles.  Ernie  spotting.  Late 2002 or early 2003.

name: The Prow
desc:
Jutting out into the air like a ship's bow, enshrouded in mystery by the cryptic elephant skin diabase texture like a vessel in the mist, sits The Prow. Technical, physical, involved and committing, this problem embodies everything of Mount Gretna and the rock type. The sit start to the Prow is my all time favorite diabase boulder problem out of all areas in Pennsylvania, a state I was born in and never left until the age of 20. I grew up on Mount Gretna Road, just a ten minute drive from the main boulder field. I have a special connection with this problem. The stand start at a stiff V5 was one of my first V5's. I completed the sit start to The Prow on April 1, 2003. I remember that day vividly. It was one of the first advanced boulder problems I had ever completed, both mentally and physically. It took me probably 7 to 10 visits to do the stand start, and by the time I was working the sit start full line a season later I was doing the stand three to five times in a day in preparation. 
 I understand that now a hold has broken and it is most certainly the crucial left hand half pad three finger sidepull crimp that has enlarged. The stand start is a sandbag or solid at the grade at V5. Right hand up anywhere you want on the arete, scrunch up, and highstep onto the blade. The right foot will be smearing on a downsloping feature, if it blows you will graze your shin on the underside of the roof. A large deadpoint for a one pad left hand sidepull immediately follows. It is the largest hold on the problem but is utilized for a very short period of time. Delicately balance your way around the right arete after more slapping, 1/3 pad sidepulls and a high right foot smear. There are at least three ways to get to the lip; technical and in control, shouldery and barndoorish, or all out dyno. I prefer the former. 
 For the full V7 or V8 sit start line that nearly doubles the length and quality of the problem, start underneath the roof blade in a true sit start and work around left on solid, almost one pad crimps. Make a very strenuous pull from a three finger three quarter pad left hand sidepull and grope up and right on the arete to a veiny pinch and swing both feet up and to the right. It may help to be short on this sequence because it is so scrunchy. High step like you would off of the ground to begin the stand start then execute the above.
location: Top of the Prow/Warm Up area.
protection: Multiple pads due to the real estate that needs to be covered rather than the height. A spotter because barn-dooring is likely. A crowd for moral support.

name: Frontslide Lipslide
desc: Start locked in with kneebars and both hands on the massive fin you would use when climbing Astroboy. Climb up the face and top out straight up.
location: Vertical fin you would use when climbing Astroboy.

name: Goofy Foot
desc:
Stand with hands matched in the seam. Move feet up and toss to the top. Find good feet and top out. 
 There is also a lower start with a tiny crimp and the arête. It doesn't add much but it could be fun to play around on. Have fun.
location: To the left of Soul Assassin V6 on the backside arête.

name: Maverick
desc: Stand start with hands matched on good holds. Find your feet and stand up to a good crimp. Bring your left foot up to the big foot and throw up to the arête just under the lip. Move your feet around and go for the top. Top out the problem.
location: When looking at Hang Ten walk around the right side of the boulder to the backside climb the arête.

name: Hang Ten
desc: Gain slab via step up to large jug. Match crimps then grab a jug and throw to the top. Kinda scary.
location: From trail 4 take the side trail leading toward Smiley and the 45. After a short walk up hill you'll come to an inobvious fork in the trail. Take the right fork. This will lead you to Soul Assasin, Hang Ten, Etc.
protection: Pad or two, but if you fall wrong they won't keep you off the slab anyway.

photos.cap: A pretty gnarly fall followed this frame.
Gaining the face on Hang Ten

name: Soul Assassin
desc: Start low with bad feet, good left sidepull and poor right hand crimp. Go big up to sloper, and fight your way to the top.

name: Wrestling Whales
desc: Start matched on a crimp seam all the way to the right of the boulder. Move left and up on the slopers, crimps and seams all the way until you round the corner to the crimps and side-pulls on the arete and mantle up using the big ledge as foot.
location: past soul assassin, keep moving right towards a small trail that goes down and you should arrive from behind the boulder towards the left side of the arete.
protection: Multiple pads, its a long traverse

name: Smiley Slab
desc: Climb up the moderate angle slab on the backside of Smiley boulder.
location: Slab on the backside of the Smiley boulder.
protection: Bouldering Pad: The landing is good although sliding down the slab on your hands and knees would be a bad idea.

name: Candy Button
desc:
Stand start the obvious arete to the left of 'Nose Picker'. Start left hand on a good side pull on the left of the arete and right on a small crimp on the right side. Pick some feet and make a long move to the good hold up and right, work your way to the good holds on the top. 
 Looks like a sit start is possible starting in the corner left of the arete. Im sure it has been done, I have not tried it however.
location: On the Smiley Boulder left of the obvious nose feature called 'Nose Picker' stand start the short arete.

photos.cap: Matt making the few moves to the top.

name: Lemon Drop
desc: Sit start, climb the dihedral
location: Immediately left of candy button

name: Smiley Face
desc: The area's namesake and a must do. Start on rail then find your way out left to positive hold. From there move up face on progressively better holds to easy slab top out.
location: Obvious problem up face of the tall boulder you come to when entering the Smiley area.
protection: Bouldering Pad: Just need one for this beauty. Excellent landing.

photos.cap: Tainiko Lowman on Smiley Face. November 2013.
The Smiley Face (v4). Mt Gretna, PA. November 2010. danallardphoto.com
Sam working the bottom of Smiley Face
Sunkook going for the intermediate off the right pinch.

name: Light Your Mind
desc:
Light Your Mind climbs the tall vertical face left and around the corner of the Smiley problem. It starts standing with a tricky long move to small crimp, which is the crux. Pick your way up crispy edges to a high top out. The rock quality on this portion of the boulder is not the best on this line, the start hold has broken since the first ascent. It may be necessary to "Light Your Mind" up with a certain substance to get into a head space where the height is not an issue, if you're into that sort of thing. 
 It is possible to avoid the tall top out by swinging around right onto the Smiley slab top out by using the large jug on the arete mid way up. Or add some length and a V grade onto the problem by starting the Smiley problem and moving left around the arete.
location: The tall vertical face of thin edges around the left arete from the heavily chalked Smiley problem.

photos.cap:
Me trying to find alternative beta to avoid the cheese grater or having to grow 5 inches.

"X" Marks the spots.

name: Smiley Right
desc: Starts on Smiley, bust up and right to a slim gaston crack. Get your foot up on the start and top out straight up.
location: Smiley Boulder

name: Nose Picker
desc: Stand start matched on the sloper and move right using two crimps before slapping the top sloper of the nose feature. Continue moving right to a good undercling, set the left foot and heel hook the right foot and go for the jug at the lip of the boulder.
location: The nose looking feature on the left side of the Smiley Face boulder.
protection:
Multiple pads, and a good spotter. 
 The landing from the crux isn't great, a spotter should be positioned to keep the climber from tumbling into the pit formed by the fallen tree and the sloping landing boulders.

name: Skate Shoes
desc: Stand start with hands on a sloper. Pull up and into the crack to work your way along. Make sure to use the giant ledge bellow you for your feet. When you get to the end of the crack find some good feet and toss for the big jug then top out.
location: Walk passed Smiley and Nose Picker up the path on the hill. About 40ft up the trail cut left and you will see a crack called Paula. Walk around the left side of the boulder and you will see a nice horizontal crack.

photos.cap: Matt setting up for the top out moves.

name: Seamstress
desc: Squat start with hands crossed and good feet. Pull up to a good crimp with your left. Bring your right up to the crimp just under your left hand. Move your feet around and Reach up high for the good crack. Stand up high and top out.
location: To the right of Paula up the hill from Smiley. The right of the two seams.
protection: Pads and spotter. Be careful of barn dooring on this one because if someone fell they could go all the way down to Paula.

name: Paula
desc: Sit in the hole match hands in the crack. Get the huge foot below you and a good smear. Smear your heart out and pull up to the good finger lock with your right. Once you get there grab the arete with your left and work your feet around. Get into a layback position to bring your right hand up high and bring your left foot up onto the arete. Rock over to your left and work up to the lip. Top out the climb.
location: Around the corner from Skate Shoes and uphill from Smiley.

name: Paulow
desc: Low start to Paula. Start with left hand in the lowest part of the crack as a side-pull. Right hand under the large undercling shelf on a crimp all the way out right. Lots of options for feet, but I used a left toe jam in a pocket and a right heel-toe cam on the shelf. Big detached block is off. Make two tensiony, powerful moves into the start of Paula. Climb up Paula as using the same finger lock and arete sequence, topping out through the dihedral.
location: Walk past Smiley and Nose Picker up the path on the hill. About 40ft up the trail cut left and you will see a crack called Paula. Walk around the left side of the boulder and you will see a nice horizontal crack.

photos.cap: Starting feet situation. Big detached block with the X's is off. The block my left foot is using is on.

name: Headnoise
desc: Slab route up, next boulder above skate shoes boulder

name: Multiple Personalities
desc: Multiple Personalities is a unique climb for Mt. Gretna. It is a traverse which is quite long and involves more than a handful of moves.Start match on slopers, or also using the crimp, on the right arete and traverse left to finish at the very end of the boulder.
location: Uphill from the Smiley Boulder on the way to Shamu.
protection: Several pads to cover the traverse. Feet get slippery near the end

name: Happy Camper
desc: Start on crimps on both sides of arete. Use heels, meat hooks, and go up arete.
location: Behind the Multiple Personalities boulder.

name: Flatliner
desc: s.d.s. with a left hand side pull and a seam for your right. move straight up to crimps and then follow the seam out right. top out as you would for "tony's roof".
location: same boulder as "tony's roof". starts on the left side of the boulder.
protection: 2 pads or one pad and a spotter to slide it along.

photos.cap: Flatliner problem: Starts to the left of Tony's roof...

name: Observable Universe
desc: Start standing on lower block, with left hand on the slopey arete and right on crimp in the center of the face. Use a decent foot hold to start and squeeze your way up the rounded boulder. Bad landing. Try not to dab the boulder to the left, but you can use it to get stood up on the lower block before establishing.
location: A few feet to the right of Tony's Roof.
protection: 3-5 pads. Fall is into uneven rocks.

name: Tony's Roof
desc: Sit start back in the roof on large, sharp underclings. Toe hook and utilize a crimpy sidepull to go again to a sloper over the lip. Other hand on a crimp over the lip, then go for the jug to an easy mantel. Used to be considered V hard but the discovery of new beta (toe hook) has made it more reasonable. Tony's Roof is one of the steepest problems in all of Gretna.
location: This problem ascends the obvious 70 degree roof along the trail 100 feet from the Smiley Boulder.
protection: Single pad, might help if it is thin.

photos.cap: Photo showing the latest break as of 3/14/25
Gonna have to try hard to get a send of this one!

name: Rocky Horror Mantel Show
desc:
The single most obvious dyno at Gretna. Start on massive horn with a perfectly placed foot hold. Hit the gritty sloper. Hold--maybe cut feet. Grab onto the multitude of jugs up there.
Crux: Top-out. Muscle-up, gripping--ripping--hooking on either the left or right side of the roof.
V8 in the guidebook--difficulty varies vastly with bodytype/strengths.
location: Left of The Outlier (v6). Past tony's roof via the left trail, up--up to see obvious horn.
protection: Two Pads, Dyno can get messy, and failed top-outs are dicey. Watch out for the left wall.

photos.cap: Horn--> Sloper. Chalked holds to the right of Rocky Horror is The Outlier (v6).

name: The Outlier
desc: Sit start matched on a obvious jug and pick some feet. Pull on and cross right hand to a sloper crimp, then work your way left to the arete. Figure out how to reach the crimp way out left from the mediocre holds of the arete. Once established on the crimp toss up and top out on jugs.
location: Follow the faint path left around the back of 'Tony's Roof" and this is the odd shaped, less than appealing looking boulder. It climbs way way better than it looks,

name: Optical Delusion
desc: Start matched on crimp rail, work your way to the top
location: Behind Paula Boulder, just uphill maybe 50’

name: Bow Hunter
desc: Start on big jug/crack on blunt arête and move straight up to positive holds above, step up and mantel.
location: Blunt arête of small boulder directly uphill from the Pulley boulder.

name: Silly Arete
desc: Start on the right side of the boulder with Pulley Mantle, and work your way up the arete.
location: Just behind the deer hunter boulder

name: Tony Danza
desc: Like Tony Danza’s talk show, this slab problem is mediocre and short lived. Climb straight up easy slab to top.
location: Start a five feet left Ninja Gaiden (left side of blunt arête) and stay on face.

name: Sumbitch
desc: An easy warm-up problem with a fun little finish. Start on right side of boulder and ride the arête to the top.
location: Right side of Shady Flake boulder.
protection: One pad directly below the finish protects this problem well.

name: Pinch Me, I’m Dreaming
desc: A fun warm up problem, with an easy top-out.Start on the lowest pinch-jug on the arete, and work your way up, topping out on the right face of the boulder.
location: Just behind the Shady Flake Boulder.

photos.cap: The Pinch Me I'm Dreaming Boulder

name: Deer Hunter (?)
desc: Sit start far right in good horizontal. Move left to good jug then crank to positive holds on rounded lip above and finish.
location: Obvious horizontal on face of small boulder directly uphill from the Pulley boulder.

name: Pulley Mantle
desc: Start on the sloper, and mantle up.
location: Just past the Deer Hunter Boulder.

name: What's it called
desc: not what I would've called it. guidebook also says it's V1, but good luck finding that beta. start with a left sidepull and right undercling, go left to slopers, and then up and left to a jug. only 3 moves to an easy top out but that 3rd move is a doozy
location: just past shady flake and some waist-high boulders in the middle of the trail linking pulley and fugitive areas
protection: ideally 2 pads to make a nice flat landing, although you're barely off the ground for the crux move

photos.cap: what's it called boulder. shady flake boulder is visible in the background

name: Ninja Gaiden
desc:
You don’t have to be a Ninja to climb this one although it would help. Start on crimps and move to a good hold at base of left trending crack. Then establish your feet and follow the crack left around arête to easier ground and top. 
 The guidebook rates this a V4.
location: Look for obvious left trending crack on downhill side of large Pulley boulder. Start below start of crack just to the right of the blunt arête.
protection: One pad to protect the opening moves then climb carefully through the easier crack section as you traverse left and up.

name: Shady Flake
desc: Start about head high on razor crimps. . . get used to them because you fight your way up many more directly up the face.

name: Foxfire Five
desc: Sit start under the mini overhang. Right hand on good flat edge, left hand on sloped undercling arete. Smear with the right and get a toe/heel hook under the arete with the left. Squeeze your way up to the jug in the crack with the left and top out.
location: Clams Casino area

name: No Man Left Behind
desc: Sit start in the pit. Right on sharp seam crimp and left on rolled crimp. Get a high foot and lock off to a good left incut then top out through more crimps and slopers at the lip.
location: Clams Casino area

name: Fugitive
desc: Stand Start with a left sidepull on the face and the highest crimp on the right arete with the right, pull on set the left foot and huck to the left arete.  Pinch the top saddle and fight to keep the right foot on as it inevitably slides off due to the dirt and moss covering the right face of the boulder and top out.
location: Triangular boulder approximately 20 yards past the Shady Flake boulder.

name: Beat Box
desc: Sit start on a left hand sidepull and a right hand edge. Fire up to a good crimp and bust to the sloper lip. Either mantle there or traverse out left and top out on the arete, either is acceptable.
location: Behind the Fugitive boulder.
protection: Lowball problem with an odd, scary landing...not sure how to spot for this problem.

name: Profile of a Fugitive
desc: The low start to "Fugitive", start low on crimps and a solid right toe hook. Pull right into better crimps, then prepare for a big dyno to the left lip.
location: Past the pulley area down a trail, low start to "Fugitive."

name: Right Bookend
desc: Follow edges up the right side of the boulder.
location: Right side of the Feel My Pain Boulder.

name: Left Bookend
desc: Layback finger crack on left side of boulder. Move up to positive holds at lip then smear your way onto slab and finish. Bring a brush to clean face.
location: 50 yards uphill from Smiley Face (V4) and just left of large boulder with Multiple Personalities (V6) traverse.
protection: Bouldering Pad: Problem is surprisingly tall but has an excellent landing.

photos.cap: Deborah Henny demonstrating the Left Bookend, V2, for the masses on a locals tour of Mount Gretna in 2002.
The delicate topout.  Also finish to the problem Hero, immediately to the right.

name: Hero
desc: Start on a crimpy seam with marginal feet. Gain slopers at the lip and mantel. Finish up the slab.
location: Left Center of the Feel My Pain Boulder. Immediately right of The Left Bookend problem.

name: Feel My Pain
desc:
Locate a line of ultra thin crimps in the center of the boulder. Start in a tiny horizontal seam with virtually no feet. Crank up to two ridiculously thin crimps. Maybe get a foot up to a miserable smear. Launch for the flat one pad edge directly above and mantel it. 
 Hideously thin, one of the crimpiest in the forest. Quite miserable, ultimately rewarding when sent. One of those problems I just had to do, because it made me so frustrated.
location: Center of the Feel My Pain boulder

photos.cap: Getting set up for the last move

name: Feel My Pain Traverse
desc: Start on 'Left Bookend' and traverse the seam and finish through 'Feel My Pain'.
location: Bookend Boulder

name: Sneaker Crack
desc: Sneakers are optional, falling is not! Climb obvious wide crack up slabby face. Either layback the crack or take it straight on. It will not present any problems.
location: From Jack in the Box head straight downhill through a narrow passage between two large boulders then cut left and head across the hillside (some easy bush-wacking required) for about thirty feet. Sneaker crack will be on your left and faces downhill.
protection: Don't even bother with a pad, you'd probably fly passed it anyway as you helplessly bounce your way down the steep hillside of boulders.

name: All Alone
desc: Stand start with jugs and climb up through the slab
location: Directly to the left of Schizophrenic

name: Tusks
desc: Stand start on a rail and climb over the small block.
location: To the right of where Under Lock And Key is.

name: Schizophrenic
desc: Stand start with a right hand on a crimp and a left on an undercling. Use the arete to work up to the top.
location: Behind the Box boulder 5 yards

name: Help Meat
desc: Several hard moves in a short space with nearly the perfect landing below, a great problem to get on if you are bouldering alone. Stand start on crimps and move up to next set of crimps then to slopers on edge. Bear down, find your feet and slap to the rim above. Top out.
location: Just to the left of the Box boulder where the access trail comes into the bottom of the area.
protection: Boulder Pad: Just one pad for this sweet guy.

photos.cap: Tim Armstrong bearing down on the slopers
If you skip the sloper out to the right, the problem is maybe easier (but less fun :).
Sinking down on the slopers on "Help Meat." [[116187507]]
Greg Sudlow reaching the sloper on Help Meat (V4). Photo by Ryan Salkeld.

name: Josh in the Box
desc:
This rig looks casual as approaching it due to it diminitive size and straight forwardness but don't be fooled this little line packs a punch! 
 Sit start on the same hold as you would for The Box (v8), put your left foot out on the large foot hold out left and press your way up to the obvious crimp 3 feet above, match the crimp and top out.
location: Just right of Help Meat (v3+), starting on the same hold as The Box (v8)

photos.cap: Yoli on Josh in the Box
The first move, which is also the crux, [[108905645]] [[116187507]]

name: Mammoth
desc: Sit start on the right side of the boulder using a jug for your left hand and a crimp for your right. Traverse going left on the lip until you reach incut holds, mantle through onto the slab.
location: Directly behind Tusk, continue right past Under Lock And Key and it will be on your left side.

name: Knuckles of Evil
desc: Sit start on left edge and right seam edge. High heel and reach up to crimp and mantle to the lip.

name: Capacitor
desc: Sit start with left hand on slim crimp, right hand on sidepull pinch under the crack. High foot, slap out left to a sloper than pull through to jug. top out from there, about 7-8 ft.Kickplate is off.
location: Trailside

name: The Box
desc: Sit start on crimp rail and go big to the box hold. Slap your way up the slopey lip and top out.
location: Box boulder

name: Under Lock and Key
desc: Start the same as Knuckles Of Evil and climb out left on really poor quality crimps. Hit the slot hold and throw for the lip.
location: If you're at the landing to Talking To Myself, continue walking back and slightly turn left into a little slice in the boulder field. There is a small cave at the end of the slice, this is where the line is located.

name: Expansion
desc: Use obvious sidepull for start hold. Work left and up topping out next to Free Time
location: Directly to the left of Free Time

name: Donkey Parade
desc: Stand start on an undercling and trend left. Top out through slopers. Be careful to not dab
location: Behind the line Free Time if you go through the opening between Free Time and Slacker.

name: One Move Wonderful
desc: Start both hands on lip with slopers and dyno for the jug lip behind.
location: 5 yards in front of Free time. Noticeable small 'cave' at bottom of boulder.

name: Slacker
desc: Start under Atavistic Drama moving right through the opening between the boulders. Finish far right.
location: Directly to the left of Free Time.

name: Atavistic Drama
desc: Stand start on arete with a right hand on sloper and left hand on an inverted feature. Go straight up onto the slab trending left and top out.
location: Left of Slacker

name: Free Time
desc: Start on a flat crimp and an incut crimp under the roof. Reach the side pull in the rough crack and jump for the coarse jugs above the lip.
location: In the One Move Boulders cluster.

name: Baby Signs
desc: Scramble up this easy arête.
location: Top of the Shamoo area. Large, blocky arete 10 feet of Heaven crack (V8).

name: Scary Face
desc: Left of shamu, obvious roof. Start on left-most jug and traverse right and top out. Slightly harder variation--dont start with the feet on the block at the bottom.
location: Left of Shamu on the roof lip.

photos.cap: Kevin O'Malley cruising it. Fun thang.
Ethan swinging through to the heel hook. Best V2 in the area. [[116174129]], [[116369012]]

name: Decepticon
desc: Technical, tall and terrific! Start on thin crimps and find your way up steep slab to finger crack then top out high above.
location: Top of the Shamoo area. Face just left of the blunt Shamoo (V6) arête.
protection: Bouldering Pads: Bring a few pads and a good spotter. There is a small tree growing near the base which could be and ankle bender on a bad fall.

photos.cap: Decepticon, to the left of Shamu.

name: Shamu Dihedral
desc:
Climb the dihedral to the left of Shamoo, on the same boulder. Start standing and lieback or stem up the slippery dihedral using a thin crack for the hands to a tall and delicate sloping lip encounter that is guaranteed to raise the heart rate. 
 Often overlooked due to the popularity of the adjacent Shamoo arete. I highly recommend this problem if you are looking for a scare similar to that of Shamoo. With good technique, this climb can be performed without much difficulty.
location: The dihedral to the left of the Shamoo arete and Heaven crack.
protection: More than one pad would be best along with a spotter.

name: Shamu
desc:
Shamoo is one of the top ten boulder problems of Mt Gretna. It embodies all of what diabase climbing is about: small holds, balance and most importantly technique. Shamoo climbs the striking seam and left arete on the most prominent boulder in the area. 
 Begin easily enough by laybacking up the left arete whilst smearing. Work your way into a position where you will be spanning between the arete and crack with your hands and no feet. 
 Hike the left foot up to nearly nothing, perch for all you are worth and reach up high left to a tiny, nearly unusable sidepull. Stomp the right smear up, no up further. Then fire out right for the opening in the crack. Hug the features for another move, then topout easily.
location: Large boulder with the striking seam Heaven (V8) and a blunt left arete. Cant miss it.

photos.cap: Steve laybacking the ultra-classic Shamoo (v5). Mount Gretna, PA. March 2011. danallardphoto.com

name: Heaven
desc:
Heaven climbs the striking seam on the Shamoo boulder. A longtime project due to its location and just beg to be climbed line. 
 Begin by pulling onto the wall with a miserable opening in the hairline seam with your left hand and right on a tiny (1/4") crimp). Cam the right foot into the bottom, wide part of the crack. Lean left and reach high to hook your right middle finger into the mono. This hold is not so much of a mono as a tooth for one finger. Left foot on the most miserable foothold imaginable. Stand onto it and reach high left hand to where the crack offsets. Begin strenuous, delicate laybacking to the topout. 
 The mono is notorious for injuring fingers, and I worry that if my left foot would skate off the smeary edge, one could lose the finger. Do not let this scare you away from the problem. The tweakiness can be mitigated by listening to your body. I have seen this climb flashed.
location: Center of Shamoo Boulder
protection: A pad or two and a spotter.

name: Balance or Power
desc:
Balance or Power is one of Dr. Torretti's top ten contributions to Mt. Gretna, and that is saying a lot. He has put up many of the best problems-especially the technical ones- (like 50-100) in this main area and at the surrounding satellite areas. 
 The climb begins sitting or crouching with hands on a large hold on the left end of the boulder. Some people will do a kind of standing start but with hands still on the hold. For full value, start sitting. Mantel this hold and reach up with the left hand to a huge sloper on a bulge. Slap around on this large feature and lean way right to grab a crimpy, inset seam which shoots straight right for ten feet. Getting established with both hands on the seam from the basketball sloper is probably the most difficult individual move, but every following move requires nearly similar exertion. Tick tac right along the crimpy seam with zero footholds. Your feet will be pawing on a steep wall for worthless smears with your butt out. After a handful of moves, you will have gained the right side of the boulder where you can mantel on a sloping lip. 
 Joel used to make this problem look graceful, and I made it look thrutchy. So the question is: balance, or power?
location: Balance or Power is on the boulder that shares it's name. This is the only problem on the large boulder. To locate it, walk uphill from Shamoo a few hundred yards. There is probably not an obvious trail leading to the boulder. A local might be needed to find it without you getting frustrated and bushwhacking. The side the problem is on faces downhill. The boulder is kind of isolated and on it's own.
protection: Two pads and a spotter would be prudent. There are vines around the boulder, and if I remember correctly, a rock in the landing midway across the seam traverse.

name: Overlord
desc: Atypical for Gretna, steep and juggy. Sit start on the obvious jug and follow the line to the top. Fun stuff.
location: In the cluster of boulders behind the 45. Take the trail toward Shamoo and look to your left.

photos.cap: Lolo busting one of the sweet opening moves on Overlord.

name: Left Handjam
desc: Start far left with a left hand jam and right slopey crimp. Has a good chip for a foot so block is off. Climb up and right to a mantle exit.
location: Far left of one move boulder

name: Overlord Arete
desc: Start holds of Overlord but get a right heelhook on the the start. Left gaston on sloping hold, tryhard to a right hand crimp and head up the arete.
location: The arete on Overlord boulder

name: Overlord Face
desc: Low start on two crimp buckets, up to crimp islands, gastogne  and finish to the knob; top out. No arete, finish straight up, dope moderate.
location: Same boulder as overlord.
protection: 2 pads for the top-out if you punt

name: Choppy
desc: Sit start, left on sloping edge, right newly broken flat crimp. Find the toe, hit the pinch sloper (hold it son), then kill it. One move wonder to good hold. Right crimp broke November, 2018.
location: In the back right area of the One Move Boulders cluster.

photos.cap: Start on left and right crimp. Next move to the pinch/sloper (quite gritty). Hold, finish. One move wonder, but challenging [[112412230]], [[116572016]]
Pre-break hold on the right. Far more incut and wide. New crimp is flatter, smaller, half a grade harder.

name: Pet Goat
desc: With your hands out left on sloppy edge, climb the long slanting slab to top.
location: Left and slightly uphill of the Talking to My Self (V1) fin.
protection: Bouldering Pads: Climb strong. The boulder filled landing is hard to protect and a slide down the slab is sure to leave a mark.

name: Talking to Myself
desc:
Sit start on low incut jugs, then follow the right arête to the top sloper edge of the boulder. Throw a high right heel and do a hard mantle to finish.
Variation:
Don’t use the arête and go straight up the face on crimps for an increase in difficulty (about 1 grade).
location: Obvious fin in the jumble of boulders at the center of the Shamu area.
protection: Bouldering Pad: Bring two pads or a spotter to protect the very end.

photos.cap: Ryan Salkeld riding the rim on the classic Talking to Myself (V1). Photo by Greg Sudlow.

name: The Talker
desc: Start on the miserable microcrimps a few feet left of Talking To Myself. Rock up on a bad right foot or reach to the big crimp flake. Bring up your feet and match the flake. Tech or dyno your way to the lip. The Talking to Myself start jugs are on for feet.
location: On the Talking to Myself Boulder, a few feet left of the eponymous problem.
protection: 2 pads, landing is bad but small.

photos.cap: Reaching for the flake from the start holds

name: Toss up to chunk
desc: Start on the triangle shaped jug-sidepull and make a big move to a jug on the lip. Proceed to struggle through a awkward top-out.
location: On the left side of the Adjustor Boulder, just right of Equilateral.
protection: 1 pad. Be careful not to block the trail.

name: Long Dong
desc: This short problem climbs the protruding boulder just left of the Adjustor boulder with it's climbs Equilateral (V7) and The Adjustor (V8). It is a short compression climb that is the only lie down start that I know of at Mt. Gretna. Lie/sit down under the roof and grasp the opposing aretes. Slap one or two moves up to the flat lip with some frustration and then mantel.
location: Adjacent left of the Adjustor boulder just off of the lower trail on the way to the Highball boulder from the Coleflesh boulder.
protection: One pad is more than adequate.

name: Off Axis
desc: I am sure this route has been done before, in the Mt. Gretna  comp it was graded V4, but V3 seems right to me. It appears as if a few holds have broken off this climb, but it still go’s from the stand start. Start on a left hand crimp, and a right hand slot/crimp-jug. Go out left to a sloper, and bump to a jug on the lip. Mantle, and do the tricky top-out.Let me know if this has another name.
location: The rightmost climb on the Adjustor Boulder.
protection: 1-2 pads, the top-out is the crux so make sure that is covered.

name: Equilateral
desc: Start on a sharp crimp on the left side of the arete and a sloper on the right, bump up through a series of crimps and slopers, eventually gwtting to a meathook jug. Top out on the main face of the boulder.
location: On the leftmost arete on the Adjustor Boulder.

photos.cap: Some of the first holds right of the arete on the boulder.

name: The Adjustor
desc:
The Adjustor is one of the better known problems of it's grade at the main Mount Gretna area, but is not one of the best quality problems. The name comes from holds breaking on the upper half after the first ascent, which required an adjustment in movement and beta and how to use the new and different handholds. The sequences and handholds went through changes for the first couple of years. Today, and for the last nine years or so, everything has stayed solid. 
 Begin by sit starting with your butt on the ground or on a single pad. The right hand is in a large, incut triangular tooth down low and the left hand on a gaston three-quarter pad edge. The starting footholds are large and flat, especially for diabase. The hips should be in close to the wall. Pull on and rock up hard on the right foot to grasp the main hold of the climb; a gaston that is held with the right hand and contains a contorted thumb catch underneath. 
 Perch the right foot on the right hand starting tooth and shove in a marginal right knee scum beneath the diagonal roof to keep you in close to the wall for when you release a handhold. Bump the left hand to a undercling on the roof feature with the elbow sticking straight up. Shift the right foot up a few inches to a good foothold. Release the right hand from the gaston to reach the right hand again high to a sloping edge feature. The middle, index and pinky fingers should go on a three finger tiny diagonal crimp that lies over a subtle sloper, while the index finger alone grabs a tiny edge that faces diagonally but at a 90 degree angle change from the other fingers, kind of like a star. 
 Keep tension and reach the left hand to a broken, third pad left facing sidepull edge with a bit of an incut. This hold is one of those that broke, but what is left now is fairly solid and good. Stand up high and run the feet up and left a bit so you can bust the right hand to the good flat lip. From here it is over, get the left hand up to a hold just beneath the lip and mantel with the right leg. 
 The whole idea of this bloc is tension. The holds are poor and none of the moves are particularly long. It is just about making intermediate movements between bad holds that all face the wrong way. If one of your appendages does not execute correctly or loses contact with the rock for more than a second, you are off. 
 All in all, this is a cool problem and you will feel great if you can figure it out. It seems so simple upon first glance, but is much more difficult than it appears. The slash grade comes from it being V8 if the features and length between the holds fit you, which seems to be about 5'11'' +/- one inch. If you are shorter like me at 5'7'', it seems harder. I don't know about tall guys over 6 foot. They may have an even easier time on it.
location: The right side, slightly overhanging face on the Adjustor boulder.
protection: One pad is adequate, no spotter necessary.

name: Teen Spirit
desc: Scramble up this surprisingly fun arête but don’t expect any edges this is friction climbing territory.
location: From the 45 Degree Area head towards the Smiley Area. Look for the large Great White boulders a short way down the trail on your left. This is the left most climb on this group of boulders.

name: Hammerhead
desc: Stand start.Start matched with hands on a sloper to your right and work your way friction climbing through slopers to top out.
location: Start with body left of the arete on the boulder just to the left of Great White.

name: Swordfish
desc: Sit start pinching arete with the left, squeezing boulder with the right and a high left heel. Can also start with the right hand on the jug on the middle face (Blue Circle). Bump up with the left, then the right, reach for a good hold on the top left of the boulder and make your way around the arete. Top out.
location: Right behind the great white boulder

photos.cap: Me at the end of the comp

name: Great White
desc: Start matched on a positive sidepull on the left-hand side arete of the boulder. Follow the slopey arete to the top utilizing some crimps on the face or huck off the marginal feet.
location: Follow the trail down the hill from the 45 boulder and Great White is 10 feet to your left.

photos.cap: Coming off the start hold of Great White, hard compression tension problem on terrible right foot.

name: Fabulous
desc: Farthest right problem on the 45. Sit start low on small pinches and make a big throw over a slopey lip to a small seam. From the seam hit the huge obvious jug then cross into another seam, mantle up and it's all over. Really fun.

name: Exhibit A
desc:
Any first time visitors eyes will be automatically drawn to this line. Two obvious holds are the only features on the 45 degree wall, the first boulder one encounters on the walk into Mt Gretna. 
 Not quite 45 degrees, this problem begs to be climbed. Begin on a sharp right hand undercling and the three finger pocket for the left hand. There is a large foot to start on. Heel or toe hook the ramp on the right and move up to the gorgeous slopers at the lip. It is possible to go with either hand. Topout on the Fabulous finishing rail. It will help if the conditions are sticky. 
 There is a great video of the first ascent on the 2001 film Hard Gret. Dynamic movement on finely grained slopers makes this a must do.
location: Right of center on the 45 degree wall.

photos.cap: F**k Char on left, Exhibit A on right

name: "23 Project"
desc: Grab the lip above the dihedral and exit.
protection: The landing is flat but slopes away so several pads and spotters are nice.

photos.cap:
Unknown/Unnamed boulder. The "Governor Dick Bouldering Guide" book does not list boulder names.

The white line is listed as "23 Project," and the black line is listed as "22 Project."

name: Pong
desc: Sit start at base of arête on solid crimps and pull to positive holds directly above. Reach for a positive crack and pull to top.
location: Pong is next to Ping or is Ping next to Pong? Either way just find the middle problem of the Ping-Pong boulders on the trail between the 45 Degree Area and the Adjuster Boulder.

name: Ping
desc: Sit start in corner with arms wide, left hand on arete and right on a good side pull, and right foot on nice edge. Shimmy up, slap the positive edge on top.
location: To the right of Pong. Located on the trail between the 45 Degree Area and the Adjuster Boulder.

photos.cap: Matt Wallace squeezing up this fun little line

name: No Biggie
desc: Right of ping, right hand end of boulder. Left hand on arete, right on low or high crimp. Right foot smear, drive up
location: To the right of ping

name: Triangle
desc: Pretty cool little problem on the side of the Ping Pong boulder. Start low on a giant triangle feature and move up through edges and slopers to a tricky topout
location: Left most problem on the ping and pong boulder
protection: A pad or two. Clean landing, good to work if you don't have a spotter

name: Slopey Feature
desc: Its all in the first move with this one. Start low on odd sloped feature, figure out your feet then pull hard with the core and pop to the good hold up high. High step and top out.
location: Boulder just up the trail from Omega Zen.

photos.cap: Tim Armstrong reaching for the jug

name: CFL
desc: Boulder up above scarlet lady boulder. Right side, start on jug and finish on slab

name: Omega Zen
desc: Clean rock, good edges and fun moves make this arguably the best in grade at Gretna.
location: 200 feet up the trail from the Adjuster Boulder, just right of the beautiful Scarlet Lady slab.

photos.cap: Tim at the top of Omega Zen

name: ESA
desc: Boulder behind scarlet lady boulder. Middle of it

name: Scarlet Lady
desc: Fantastic slab dancing. Find the sequence up the face and keep it together at the top.
location: Down the hill from the 45. Shares the same boulder as Omega Zen
protection: ~3-4 pads and a spotter are a good idea. It's sort of tall and the landing's less than ideal. You'll wanna cover that tooth at the bottom real well

name: Toxic Toys
desc: Start left hand on a high side pull, right hand on the arete. Establish solely on the face with small feet edges. Position yourself and make the move to the top jug.
location: The boulder to the left of Scarlet Lady.
protection: Lots of pads. Barn doors and foot slips can send you pinging off in any direction. Got a bruised heel and shoulder from missing the pads twice in a row.

photos.cap: What was once a soft v7 called corporate strategies, now broken and possibly unclimbed

name: Cheap Shot
desc: Start under the roof right on a good undercling. Using detached block for feet, traverse left and reach for the edge of the roof. Pull up and grab a spine like feature that leads to the jug and mantle up.
location: Just downhill of “Scarlet Lady"

name: Pickin' the Bone
desc: Starts with a low left hand, right hand on right slopey feature. Smack up and left to a good slopey edge. Top out from there.
location: Below Scarlet Lady, and to the left.
protection: only a few crash pads necessary.

name: "Trailside Project"
desc: Slopers and small feet lead to mantle exit
location: Small blunt boulder adjunct to trail, about 100ft from 45 Degree Wall.
protection: Given the diminutive stature of the boulder and flat landing, a pad is nice but optional.

name: Baby Tortoise
desc:
Fun problem, traverse the overhanging side of the Tortoise boulder from right to left, starting on a jug and working through interesting holds to a fun top-out, if you go the opposite way, it is V3.
Great problem to do laps on to prep for some of the harder climbs nearby.
location: Follow directions to the Adjustor Boulder, then the Tortoise Boulder, with the Baby Tortoise Problem will be on your right.
protection: No pad necessary if you can easily climb V1-2

name: Eco Depot
desc: Start on the obvious flat mega jug, make a big move to the arete, move your left hand to a jug, and top-out.
location: Just above the Adjustor Boulder, and just below  Scarlet Lady V4.

name: Storage Unit
desc: Start low on the right arete, and work your way up.
location: Just above the Adjustor Boulder, and just Below Scarlet Lady V4.

name: Ikea
desc: Start with 2 sidepulls, and move out left to the arete, proceed with some easier moves to a fun and easy top out.
location: Just to the right of the Chungus boulder.

name: HighBall Crack
desc: climb the crack on the back of the highball
location: to the right of the squeak

photos.cap: left side of highball crack (right side blocked by tree)

name: The Original Route
desc: This line begs to be climbed. There is a tempting jug a few feet from the summit. Climb up thin, incut crimps and sidepulls on the vertical face to reach said alluring hold and the final flake. In 2000 it was more like V1 but holds have broken.
location: Obvious tall face you will first see when approaching the boulder.

photos.cap: Nate getting high and sticking the three finger crimp on "The Original Route"
The Original Route is on the left side of the rock here

name: No One's Getting Any Younger
desc: Stand start the right side of the north arete and go up using delicate smears and edges.
location: This is the left-most route on the boulder's north slab, and another amazing moderate highball on the Highball Boulder.  While it shares the arete with Kundalini, it climbs in a completely different style--sort of like a mellower version of Shamu.
protection: Pads. Note that it's possible to fall quite far off the left side of the arete.

name: Delerium Tremens
desc: Delerium Tremens is the alluring east arete. Begin on the sidepulls at head height. High step, lock off on the gaston and reach to an edge. Get established on the face and climb up crimps leading to the obvious pinch on the arete. Snag the lip with the aid of a crimp on the other wall. The topout is easy, thankfully. The crux is the first move and gets progressively easier the higher one climbs. Until 2003 or so there was a tooth on the initial gaston that make it easier but more painful.
location: Right arete when looking at the main steep face of the highball boulder.

name: Brady Arete
desc:
The Brady Arete is the prominent steep arete to the right of The Original Route and connects with "Original Route" at the Thank God jug 3/4 the way up the boulder. It is certainly the most serious highball in all of Mt. Gretna. Joel Brady caused quite a stir among us locals when he completed this long eyed project during a visit around 2004. Not only is it incredibly highball and proud, but a pointed rock lies embedded in the ground directly underneath the fall zone. 
 Start standing and climb up to a flat jug on the corner around ten feet up. Take a deep breath, then begin the horrifying journey up the next fifteen feet through rarely traveled terrain. The right face is flaky and not the best rock quality. On the plus side, it is peppered with tiny flaky edges. The upper portion appears to utilize the arete for both hands in some spots, and the left hand on the arete with right hand on edges on the right face in other areas. 
 It would be prudent to clean the rock on toprope before attempting, as I am certain the climb has not been tired in quite some time. Better yet, work the boulder on a top rope before bouldering it out. Think of it as a headpoint. Or the best idea may be to skip this climb and move on to a problem that will not risk broken ankles or worse. 
 If you send this boulder, you have serious street cred in my mind. I imagine it has seen only a handful of ascents in the ten years after its first ascent. The Brady Arete is one of the most risky undertakings that I have seen out of all of the diabase areas, save for a few of Char's creations at Haycock. Only The Yosemite Crack (V10) at Haycock comes to mind as a rival in terms of height and fall potential.
location: Arete right of the narrow side of the boulder containing The Original Route. The left arete when looking at the wide face that is tall, flaky and steep.
protection: Pads. Many, many pads. Oh, and spotters. Or a top rope for the sane.

name: Highball Slab
desc: Start on a large high right foot and move up using friction and intricate footwork to a final dynamic move to a flat edge, then top out.
location: On the backside of the highball boulder.

name: The Squeak
desc: start left on the small foot ledge on the back slab of the highball, and work your way right and up on smears and crimps. very tricky.
location: back of the highball boulder

name: Kundalini
desc: Sit start the technical and physical sloping arete, using small crimps on the left face.
location: This is the left side of the imposing north arete of the Highball Boulder.  (The north arete forms the left side of the boulder's smooth slab face.)  This is a tall problem with an uneven landing, though it gets easier toward the top.

photos.cap: Kundalini is the near face and right-hand arete. [[116775009]]

name: The House of Cards
desc: Stand start right of center on a large hold.  Climb up on small crimps, trending slightly left, then back right.
location: This is the majestic east face of the highball boulder.

photos.cap: The House of Cards is in the middle.

name: Agrobat
desc: start on the right side of the lowball rock on the side of the trail. work your way around and left using heel hooks, snag a crimp and mantle.
location: on the path just before the highball

photos.cap: Slovenia's finest HB, Andrew Kissler, taking a typical factor-2 neckbreaking whipper on the first bolt on arguably the finest lowball stair-stepper on the east coast.

name: Mini Saucer
desc: Sit Start on the right side of the boulder with hands on the lip, traverse the lip and mantle.
location: The smallest boulder in the first cluster of boulders

name: Rainbow Goat
desc: Stand start using a sidepull and undercling move up the the slopers at the lip and mantle.
location: Left of Momentary Lapse of Reality.

name: Mic Check
desc: Feature slab with right slanting crack. V0 any way you do it. Sit Start makes it better but no harder.
location: Downhill side of the boulder opposite of gladiator.

name: Chunky Monkey
desc: Almost certainly climbed before but unlisted in the guide. Start hanging off the chunky arete and climb up using the featured corner
location: Directly downhill of Mic Check

name: Every Saucer Has A Silver Lining
desc: Sit start on the left side of the boulder on a jug below the lip.  Move up to the lip and traverse the lip and top out on the far right side of the boulder using a jug.
location: The biggest boulder in the first cluster of boulders in the Gladiator Area.

name: Munkey Tongue
desc: Almost certainly climbed before but unlisted in the guide. Sit start hanging matched on the lowest good edge left of the arete, with a very high heel. Climb straight up.
location: Left of Chunky Monkey.

name: Your Pet Name Here
fa: Jason L, Roxanna Taginya, Craig Helbig
desc: Start with two hands on the arete. Find good feet and move to the top.There's potential for a low start too. Could go at a V2-3.
location: Find the boulder that's between MLoR and 2 Inch Pinch. Then go behind the boulder.

photos.cap: Side view of Your Pet Name Here

name: Lefty Loosey
desc: Fun moderate with comfy holds, some spanny moves for the vertically challenged but feet and friction are provided. Starts on good undercling and make big move up and left to good sidepull and pull up to topout.
location: Undercling start a couple feet left of Momentary Lapse of Reality.

name: The 2 Inch Pinch
desc: Lowball overhang climb. See guidebook for better description, I am posting it here for logging purposes.
location: If you are facing Momentary Lapse of Reality, turn around and you'll see this lowball. Maybe a 15 second walk from Momentary.

name: Gladiator
desc: Sit Start either matched on a crimp or right hand on lower crimp. Hard move to pocket at bottom of the seam. Go up through crack and crimps and finish left to a jug. If you go right to flat hold for the finish its a v7
location: Gladiator Boulders

photos.cap: KT C on the starting holds of Gladiator. Crimp to the right is also on for a starting hand.
KT C on the starting holds of Gladiator. Crimp to the right is also on for a starting hand.

name: Momentary Lapse of Reality
desc: Sit start on crimps and move right through more crimps towards the tree, slap the slopers at the lip and mantle.
location: The second last boulder in this area, this boulder features a tree growing right next to it on the right.

name: Temporary Temptation
desc: Start on the two obvious crimps (same start as momentary lapse of reality) then move up and left to a sharp sidepull crimp, work the feet and reach high for a classic beach whale top out.
location: Same start holds as momentary lapse of reality. Instead of going right on the boulder, go left and up.

photos.cap: The general path of Temporary Tenptation

name: Momentary Lapse of Reality Low
desc: Stat with left on undercling and right hand on good sidepull, paste feet, and pull up to start of Momentary Lapse of Reality and traverse up and right on obvious crimps. Tricky topout.
location: Start is just beneath the start of Momentary Lapse of Reality

name: Temporary Temptation Low
desc: Sit start low with left hand on undercling and right hand on good sidepull. Paste feet and make way to the starting crimps of momentary lapse of reality and Temporary Temptation, then finish left and up on Temporary Temptation.
location: Start is just beneath the start of Momentary Lapse of Reality

name: The Keystone
desc: Lay down start on the right side of the boulder, matched on a ledge with a right heel hook. Climb up great edges to slopers on the lip. Continue left to top out same as The Capstone.
location: Just off of the 15 trail to the right.

name: The Capstone
desc: Sit start on small boulder at left arete, with two crimps just above a flat triangle hold. Do a big move to a large sloper, then traverse the lip right on crimps to the center of the boulder for a nice top out.
location: Just off of the 15/diamond trail, to the right.

name: Trickle in Time
desc:
Trickle in Time is Chet Gross' first masterpiece and probably the most revered problem in all of Mt. Gretna. It climbs the subtle sloping lip of a steep roof and in true diabase style; surprisingly finicky and technical despite the severe overhang. A testament to Chet's ability to envision problems from seemingly unclimbable features. 
 Start sitting on the rail. Heel hook and head for the triangle shaped hold, which is more of a feature than a hold, that you will utilize for both hands in the near future. This problem will work your right hamstring. Get established on this hold (will help if it is cold and not humid), match with a gaston-ish meat wrap grip and make a dynamic move to snag the two and a half finger crimp. Now you need to attain the sidepull/crack/fingerlock thing with a go-again. A tiny foot lies far under the overhang for the left foot to aid in the transition between crimp and crack. 
 The crux is over, toe hook the left foot on the starting rail which will allow you to hook your right heel over your hand (probably the only time I have ever had to do this on diabase) to grope the right hand up your choice of a blank wall around the corner or a sharp arete, aiming for the apex of the arete with the top of the boulder that forms a nice pinch. A right knee scum is possible. Pull around the right face, traverse the lip and topout. This problem has been done as an eliminate without using the crack and is most likely V9 that way. 
 Trickle in Time is the problem that almost everyone considers the benchmark for V8 at Mt. Gretna. It is a problem that feels impossible until one works out the subtitles. In optimal conditions with low temperature and humidity, this problem feels easier. (in my opinion it could be a sandbag V6 at one or two granite bouldering areas I can think of). A guaranteed full body workout.
location: Not in sight of the Highball boulder. Walk past the Highball into the woods. There is a faint trail. Skirt along the level terrain at the base of the hill which leads to the Matrix for a few hundred meters, heading slightly downhill. the boulder is by itself and the problem is on the far side of the face as one approaches, it is fairly nondescript. Look left at the first large boulder you encounter and you will see a striking overhang.
protection: A pad or two, it will help if one is thin due to dab potential.

photos.cap: Matthew Bashista completing the boulder problem Trickle In Time three times in one session.

name: Truth or Dare
desc: Follow the left arching arete using a shelf, and then mossy smears for feet. Slopey topout, with one specific notch for a couple fingers.
location: Pass the highball area, then cross the creek and walk another ~100yards. This route is in the large cluster of boulders on the left side of the trail just before the trail for Trickle in Time. Squeeze past a tree to get behind the main boulders to find this route tucked in a little crevice.

name: The Hole
desc: Start matches on crimp rail in cave. Do a big move out left to a huge side pull, then squeeze through the hole without dabbing
location: Left of Chark Attack

name: Chark attack
desc: Match crimp side pull in middle of concave face. Use bad feet and pop to a finger jug and top out
location: Middle face

name: Particle Man
desc: Use flakes and crimps to move up this short slab.
location: Short slab left and around the arete from the Reunion seam.

name: Shroom Star
desc: Sit start on crimps, move up to sloppers then high step and pull for top. Good diversity for a short problem.
location: Backside of the Reunion boulder.

name: Porcelain
desc: A beautiful problem and a slab lover’s dream. Climb straight up center of face on delicate holds. Fantastic!
location: Enter the Upper Matrix area, this slab problem takes center stage and can’t be missed.
protection: Bouldering Pad: One large pad will do.

photos.cap: looking down Porcelain at Mt. Gretna
