name: Needle to the Vein
desc: Fun one move wonder near Porcelain. Start on bad hands and a bad foot and make a long move to a not great hold. From there, hit the jug and top out
location: When facing Porcelain, this problem starts on the arete of the boulder directly to your left.

name: Reunion
desc: Route shares boulder with Needle to the Vein. Start with right hand in the seam and left on the arete. Go up.

photos.cap: Tim Armstrong squeezing up this awesome v5.

name: Turtle in a Half Shell
desc: Start matched on interesting pinches at waist height. Campus or use high feet for a hard first move to good edges just at the lip of overhang. Climb the cool turtle shell face with some big moves to good holds at the top.
location: Next boulder over from Jolie (V8).

photos.cap: Pic taken a few feet from the start

name: Jolie
desc: Sit start matched on a flat jug, make big moves left onto crimps and use tricky beta to move around the blunt arete.  Reach up and grab a hold that forms the corner with the porcelain slab and top out, it is a little spooky near the top.
location: The trail 15 side of the porcelain boulder when approaching from Trail 15.

photos.cap:
Jolie
Start jug is circled.
The holds were caked in chalk when I arrived the day this photo was taken. Please remember to thoroughly brush your ticks and chalk off the holds before you leave a boulder!

name: The Green Marble Arete
desc: Climb the left arete of the Green Marble boulder. Start by stepping up onto a rock at the base to gain jugs. Make long moves to grab the left facing flake and then the flat top of the flake. All of the holds are huge. Then a big move to the juggy lip. This problem is in my opinion the best easy highball in all of Mt. Gretna! It is characterized by long moves to big gym style holds to a tall but easy top out. The grade is about 5.9+ or easy 5.10.
location: Walk past the Year Of The Dragon. The Green Marble is the obvious massive boulder uphill.
protection: Pads, spotters, or do not fall.

name: The Green Marble
desc: The Green Marble (Direct) route starts on the left arete of the Green Marble boulder. Climb the start of the Green Marble Arete route (the left arete) by stepping up onto a separate small rock underneath. Gain the left facing flake low, then bust right to the hanging jug rail that lies over the bulge. Go right for another move to a finger bucket with the right hand and highstep the left foot and mantel to the juggy lip. A real hair raiser!
location: Uphill and a bit further down the trail past the Year Of The Dragon (V6).
protection: Pads, spotters, or better yet do not fall.

name: Year of the Dragon
desc:
Year of the Dragon is a bit of an anomaly for Mt. Gretna. It climbs a slightly overhanging face on, gasp, actual holds! Plus, the sequence is not cryptic. 
 Start sitting on two crimps. Backstep and work up solid, small crimps to the obvious, beckoning sloping pinch. This hold is one of the best in all of Mt. Gretna. Slap out left around the slight corner to a sidepull. Keep it together and squeeze the right arete to topout. 
 I always felt that it helped to be tall for this problem. I could never keep my feet on while moving from the pinch, while I watched Ernie have no problem with it over and over. I consider this a benchmark problem for V6 at Mt. Gretna. Of course, that is assuming optimal conditions. The pinch will feel impossible to hang onto in the summer. There is an excellent video of this problem on the 2001 film Hard Gret.
location: Walk 100 meters past the upper and lower matrix. Year of the Dragon will be on your right just off the trail, and the problem will face your back. The boulder is downhill of the large Green Marble boulder.

photos.cap: Getting into the business of the climb
Kelly working Year of the Dragon
Great climb thats with you until the end.
Rocky working Year of the Dragon

name: Crouching Tiger
desc:
Start matched on a big flat side pull with feet wide right to a vertical edge. Drop left to the crimps and reposition feet to shoot to the top. Various options--tiny u-shaped micro-crimp, slopers wide left and on top. A little contrived.
Good practice for diabase top-outs
location: Line is left of Year of the Dragon v6

photos.cap: Upper Matrix: Crouching Tiger and Year of the Dragon

name: The Breadloaf
desc: This problem sits front and center and just begging to be climbed! Stand start on far left of the boulder and traverse across finger crack topping out at the far right.
location: Large boulder at top of area with obvious crack up high.
protection: A pad and an attentive spotter to scoot your pad along as you traverse.

photos.cap: Deborah Henny setting up and executing the cross through to a rare pocket at Mount Gretna on The Breadloaf V3, 2002.

name: Claddagh
desc: Sit start underneath the crack to the right of Samhain. Pull on using the obvious jug to the right, throw your feet up and jam them into the crack. Work some trickery to get right-side up, then finish up the crack to the top.
location: Lower Matrix, next to Samhain.

name: Lonely Boy
desc: Stand/Squat start in an awesome corridor down from "Crazy Game of Poker". Follow the only pure holds all the way up and out of the corridor WITHOUT touching the rock behind you for the full value! If you "DAB" the top out by touching the rock behind you, its like the rock has your spot, but makes it a little easier! Another CLASS-SICK Problem for the already cool Lower Matrix Area, F.A.'ed by John Carriere!
protection: Just need a Crash Pad, and follow the path of the really cool holds up both sides of the arete!

name: Spring Chicken
desc: There are several excellent cracks in the lower Matrix, but this one is the longest, the hardest, and the scariest. I am not sure what you call a sit start below ground level in a cave, but suffice it to say you start quite low. Jam your way up to where it gets wide and you can jam no more; them layback the offwidth until you can top out through the hole in the roof. The jammy part is pretty casual because the ground follows you up as you climb out of the hole so the fall isn't much of a concern; the layback however has the potential to dissect you in half should you peel off. It is suggested that a pad be used to cover the obvious giant axe feature. The rating is debatable, a crack climber would probably call it 5.11. A visiting climber from the Czech Republic for example flashed it and said it was the funnest thing he had climbed in Pennsylvania, while local bouldering mutants were unable to get off the ground.
location: In the deepest bowls of the Matrix. Get down into the caves and at the bottom of the deepest hole is an overhanging hand crack which comes up into an offwidth that climbs up through an opening to the daylight above.
protection: Taping of hands is advised, its a bit course. Spotter holding a pad above the sharp rock.

photos.cap: Spring Chicken. Not a great photo but its not a very photogenic route.

name: Crazy Game of Poker
desc: Start in the hole and climb out on surprisingly good for Gretna holds.
location: Lower Matrix, beside Breadloaf
protection: A bunch of pads and a spotter. The landing and fall are a little hairy

photos.cap: Matthew Bashista on Unnamed (V6) in the Matrix area on a pre-planned day of completing 10 different classic hard Mount Gretna problems considered sandbag V5-8.
The opening business on Crazy Game of Poker
High on Crazy Game of Poker
The deceptively hard beginning to Crazy Game of Poker

name: Samhain
desc: Start on right face crimps around face height  near the right arete. Move left into crimps before a tricky top out.
location: Lower Matrix. the backside of Crazy Game of Poker through the tunnel.

name: Downramp
desc: Good climb for little kids or good way to downclimb off the boulder.
location: On the opposite side from Modest Man.

photos.cap: Gillian warming up at the comp

name: Modest Man
desc: A jug-o-licious romp whose only problem is its over too quick.
location: First problem you will come across when bushwacking up from the access trail.

name: Transform
desc: Slightly harder than its sister climb Transform but soft for the grade. Start in crack then slap out left and then up.
location: Five feet right of Modest Man in the first part of the Mojo Area.

name: Mojo Inhibitor
desc:
Start by sitting and grasping a sloping edge with the left hand and an opposing sloping feature pinch with the right hand. Bust up and left to a sloper. If you're short--come right back into the right crimp on the middle of the face.
Work up and perch on a right then transition to a left heel hook on the left hand starting hold to reach sharp holds up on the angle change of the arete. 
OR 
Dig left toe under the roof on left collection of nubbins. Throw hard to the left crimp, then deadpoint toss from there straight to jug on arete.
Follow the arete up an easy low angled finish. This is an amazing compression problem.
*Start beta - People have started this boulder with a right heel and a right hand on the starting hold--The guidebook suggests starting with only the hands on. Do whichever, great pebble.
location: The main proud difficult looking bulge/prow in the center of the Mojo area.
protection: A pad or two will be helpful for the work it will take to solve this problem.

photos.cap: Jacob Woods, Left on sloper, right on start hold, coming into the intermediate crimp--left perched on nubbins below the roof. KEEP THE TENSION--PssSSAH!
Mojo Inhibitor on left, Mossy Slab on right

name: Roller-coaster
desc: Squat start with hands matched on a good hold. Pick some feet and pop up to a good crimp with your left, bring your right hand up and match. Swing up to the lip and pull over for the top out.
location: On the same boulder as Zipper, the right most route.

name: The Zipper
desc: Stand start with a good left hand and a slopey right. Work your right foot up to a good smear. Zip to the top with your right hand and latch the good lip. Bring your feet up and top out.
location: Just below Crimptonite to the left of Rollercoaster.

name: The Shadow Gallery
desc: Stand with your hands matched on a small but good crimp. Pull up and rock over the good foot out left, lock in your core and reach up and match on a good set of crimps. From here get ready to commit to the crux, gently move up to the slopers while moving your feet up, just when you think you are going to pop make a quick move to the jug at the lip.
location: In a corridor about 6ft right of Main Attraction

photos.cap: The sweet feeling of latching the jug
Coming out of the shadows and onto the slopers
On the slopers hoping the friction is good!

name: Crimptonite
desc:
Stand start the two lowest crimps in the diagonal seam. Bump up to a decent crimp and get ready and toss up to the slopers at the lip. Pick some feet and go for the crimps up and left. Throw a heel up and top out. 
 There is a low start on a left hand crimp and a sharp right hand crimp throwing up to the rail that has been done.
location: On the boulder above and a little left of Rollercoaster and Zipper.

name: The Main Attraction
desc: Start on juggy side pull and go up and left on good holds above the slab. Top out using the cruxy flared vertical crack via layback, jams, and crimps. A bit dabby, but only on the easy section.
location: In the cave uphill and to the right of Crimptonite. 40.25500˚N, 76.44020˚W
protection: A thin pad and a strap to hold it in place was nice to put on the slab and another pad for the start.

name: Fury Road
desc: Sit start as for Mad Max. Work your way up and right to top out to the right of the roof, on good holds.
location: On the arete of The Roof boulder

name: Mad Max Direct
desc: Stand start on two incut crimps above head height. Throw up to a good hold with your right rearrange your feet and grab the good hold with your left. This is where it gets a little spicy. Pull up and lock off with your left and reach up high for a good crimp above the lip. Find the feet and rock up to two more crimps. Climb the slab to the top.
location: In the middle of the roof.

name: Mad Max
desc: Sit start matched on a big jug with a heel hook and throw right to a good sidepull. Move your feet around and toss to a decent left crimp. Bring your heel in closer to you and reach up for a small right crimp. Relax yourself a little and bump your left to a higher crimp. Find some good feet and prepare to shoot up to an ok hold with your right. Once you are here work your way left into the top out of Mad Max Direct.
location: On the arete of The Roof boulder just to the right of Mad Max Direct.

name: White Room
desc: Start matched on a small pointy jug at stomach height with feet on the block under the main boulder. Climb straight up.
location: Far left edge of King Louie Boulder

name: Runnel
desc: Start matched on the shelf/jug at the bottom of the enticing dihedral. Move up to get feet on the shelf and using the crack for hands, use a smear on the right to walk feet up a bit unti you can reach generous jugs at the lip.
location: The central dihedral on the King Louie boulder

name: Grand Strategy
desc: Stand start in the capped corner using a chunky hold to stem and get established. Work up through opposed flakes and move slightly left to stand up to slopers on the lip. There is a deep seam pocket to help topping out about a foot behind the top lip.
location: Capped corner on the right side of the King Louie boulder.

name: Flying on a cloud
desc: Shorter problem with a sloped landing on the far right side of the King Louie boulder. Sit start matched on good flat edge with ok feet, then make moves right to a decent sidepull crack. re-establish and slap up left to a big flat sloper. Stand up and find the good seam pocket to topout.
location: Far right side of the King Louie boulder

name: King Louie
desc: Climb the smooth subtly featured slab between the dihedral and capped corner utilizing the right arete and crimp seams.
location: Central to the King Louie boulder.

name: Big Pimpin'
desc: Sit start with left on knob and right on good side pull. Compress your way up the boulder. Start start on left pinch and right in the seam goes at V5.
location: The main face of the green slab boulder
protection: a few pads and a spotter

photos.cap: Does anyone know if either of these feet are on for the start?

name: Finger Fun
desc: This is the hand crack formed by the meeting point of the central and rightmost boulder in the Beautiful Day cluster. It's probably 5.7ish, has a few rad hand jams, and is pretty darn amazing. Just make sure you're solid, because like all the other problems here it's quite tall. If you don't know how to jam it's going to be significantly harder.
location: Obvious hand crack to the right of the tall slab of the central boulder in the cluster.

name: Right Arete
desc: The area warm up. Start sitting on the lower block, move out the roof, mantle on the boulder, and up the mossy slab/arete. Just put your feet where the green ain't. Not as scary as the rest of the problems here, and not a bad beginner route.
location: Far right arete of the rightmost boulder in the beautiful day area.
protection: Pads/Spotters. The ground rises along the right side of the climb.

name: Brady Arete
desc: Another great problem ascending the arete of the boulder to the right of Beautiful Day. Start on obvious holds and work your way up the arete then transition onto the slab and top it out. It's possible to bail onto the beautiful day boulder if you get sketched, but i think the hardest moves are lower. That being said it's scary as hell up there.
location: Left Arete of the center boulder in the B-Day cluster. Next problem to the right of Beautiful Day.
protection: a few pads and spotters. it's tall and if you blew it at the top i think the fall would be weird.

name: Beautiful Day
desc: The reason you'd come to this area. Start matched on obvious high start hold and work your way through crimps and gastons to a jug, then make a long reach high to a side pull and on to an easy top out. Great Problem!
location: If you're looking at the boulders, this is the face on the left
protection: A few pads and spotters. The landing is okay but the problem is pretty tall

photos.cap: Standing up into good side pull

name: Sick Slab
desc: I'm not 100% sure about the grade on this one. If you go straight up the slab and stay away from either arete, which are both their own seperate problem, then i think it's not only hard but horrifying as well. Get's 800 comp points if that's any indication of the grade, which i'm not sure it is. If you bail out right toward the top it's a little more managable but still has quite a pucker facctor.
location: The tall, proud slab of the central boulder in the Beautiful Day Cluster.

name: Slice
desc:
Stand start on a low foot rail and use small crimps for hands. Step up on the crimp rail and move out left. Slap up the side to reach a small crimp. Topout from here. 
 Note: the crimps will wear on your fingertips - the name says it all!
location:
Bottom of the Bulge area, located on the edge of a dropoff. 
 From Shamu Area: Follow the trail NE (to the right if you're looking at Help Meat and The Box in Shamu area). It's the first large boulder after passing the main Bulge trail (on the left). 
 From Smiley Area: Follow the trail that wraps around the left side of the Smiley boulder. Keep right on the trails. You should see a long boulder to the left (Multiple Personalities), stay right and go uphill to the Bulge. Slice will be on the right. Warning: you may end up in the Shamu area if you take a left trail on the uphill portion after the Mult-P boulder. 
 From the Education Center: Follow interpretive trail to second three-way split (trail 4). Go right. At the next split, go left onto trail 15. Follow the trail to the second post on the left at approx. 450 yards (first post on the left is 45 Area; second post on the left is Smiley Area). Follow directions from Smiley Area.

name: Bashista Yo Sista
desc:
A cool, powerful, intricate climb. To send this climb specific beta is what you KNEED. 
 Sit start or squat if you cannot reach the starting holds. Start right hand in a good single pad undercling and left on the sloper rail. Move up the narrow block compressing with your whole body until you hit the good hold on the lip, from here climb around the right side of the block to a tough top out. 
 This would get 4 stars however, the close proximity to the rocks on either side make it less than classic because of the dab potential. 
 Also apparently on the FA it was topped out fairly straight on but that feels very contrived and after talking to several locals the new standard and most natural line is to top out on the right side. When I climbed it I found this to be the most natural way, topping out straight up takes away from the quality of this great line.
location: From 'The Box' walk up the hill and to the right, pass 'The Bulge' and when you pass that boulder look left into a corridor and you will see this line.

rh crimp to lh sloper. nice roc
Getting into the meat of the climb

name: The New Girl
desc: Climb the small overhang to the right of Bashista Yo Sista from a jug on the point of the lip. Bottom boulder is not utilized.
location: about 20 feet to the right of Bashista Yo Sista

name: 1st & Last
desc: Sit start matched in vertical crack with a high right foot, move up to a nice right facing sidepull. Work up to seam, then left to a far edge on face.
location: Last boulder on the trail after Bashista Yo Sista.

name: Squeezematic
desc: Sit start with a left hand on the left arete, and right hand in a good ledge on the right side of the bulging feature. Wrestle your way up the boulder to a good gaston crimp, pull and top out from there.
location: Bashista Boulders. Left of Bashista Yo Sista.

Kevin O'Malley eyeing the first move before putting it down.

name: The Lieback
desc: Sit start climbing the obvious crack,
location: Offwidth crack that is located under and right to The Bulge

name: Josh's Bulge
desc: Sit start under roof in a really good crack. Climb up the face utilizing crimps.
location: To the right of The Lieback. There is a low block that you will put pads on.

name: Paper Tiger
desc: Stand Start with a right hand crimp near the arete and a left hand crimp at your waist. Get high feet and go to a sidepull. Top out left onto slab. Be careful with the fall. Bring a blubber pad or a half pad.
location: Directly left to The Bulge. Small Block right where you would want crashpads to be.
protection: 2 pads, a blubber or half. Bring a spotter

name: The Bulge
desc: Stand start with a sloper for your left and a crimp edge far right. You'll have two pretty good feet, shorter people tend to have some beta issues reaching the left. Shoot big to a good sidepull and throw a heel to work through the seam trending right. Once you get to the horizontal part of the seam mantle and begin the non gimme top out on the slab still trending right.
location: Obvious massive bulge boulder.

name: Jungle Cat Disco Challenge
desc: Start on a crimp, and a right facing crimp-sidepull, move left to the crimp seam, make a reachy move to the solid holds in the seam on the middle of the boulder (make sure to avoid the jugs above until you have both hands in the seam crimps), move up to big jugs, and make an easy top-out.
location: When on top of the Clutch Boulder, this will be on the left side.
protection: 1-3 pads depending on how hard you climb. The landong for the top-out could be a bit weird if you fall.

photos.cap: The whole slab wall next to Clutch

name: Don't Blink
desc: Start sitting on the right side of the boulder with sidepull and nice crimp edge. Go up to nice holds and finish the top out with the seam. Alternate start uses a small sloping edge to the left of the crimp.
location: Directly off trail 15, just before the trail 4 intersection on the left if coming from the Clutch boulder.

name: Clutch
desc: Start left on sloping on the left side of the boulder. Right on crimp (Freshly broken 11-2018). Move feet and hands to big seam--then finish with giant undercling.
location: Clutch boulder--face.

photos.cap: Sunkook on pre-break clutch--hitting intermediate and about to deadpoint the crux hold. Bottom starting right crimp snapped off in a mighty event by Kevin O'Malley.

The Italian Bungaloid spraying about the real crux-- life.

name: Masterpiece Mockery
desc: Start on a left hand undercling and a round stone for the left hand. Go straight up on rounded crimps.
location: The climb in the middle of the wall.

name: Gravity Committee
desc:
Traverse the lip right to left, starting at the far corner. Top out at the peak.
If you liked "Every Saucer has a Silver Lining", this is another good one.

name: The Lemmings
desc: Sit start on coarse jug with a left heel around the corner. Climb up the arete using good face holds and a bad left sloper.
location: The left arete of the Lemmings boulder

name: Bird of Prey
desc: Sit start on the right side of the jug rail. Make a big shouldery move to a slimper with an incut thumb catch. Either come into a side pull with the left (as the guide says) or rip it straight to the top as a 1, 2, paddle dyno. The guide says something may have broken at somepoint. As of 05/2022 the holds seem solid.
location: On the right side of the Lemmings boulder.

name: Flying Monkey
desc: Sit start under triangular arete with left on razor crimp and right on undercling jug. Smear and climb up slopers, topping out on the left side of the arete. Topping out the right side is not as fun.
location: Probably the first boulder you will see in this area. Right off the bouldering trail on your left.

name: Swiss Spine Surgery
desc: LH on crack sidepull and RH on microcrimp. Stand up on slopey feet and climb up small crimps to the horizontal crack before finishing right of tree & in the center of the slab.

name: All Over You
desc: Hang start with lowest good sidepull for right and a lower two finger crimp for the left. Throw out to a jug sidepull and undercling. Then finish up the tall slab with left running crack to jugs way up.I recommend climbing up the dead tree and standing on it to brush out the crack and the top out. It is mossy and accumulates dirt.
location: Go downhill and right after you get on the bouldering trail.

name: Style Wars
desc: Sit Start left hand on a sidepull and an incut hold for your right. Go up and shoot far left following cracks.
location: First line you encounter coming into the Chickenhawk area. There is a more incut area to put your feet for relation.

name: Pigs in Zen
desc: Sit start on a slanting edge. Match the seam and do some big moves up and right to a nice edge.
location: Arete to the right of Chickenhawk

name: Elements
desc: Sit start on a triangle block and using low block for feet. Go to a bulge feature with slopers on it and mantle.
location: Back in 'cave' on the left side.

name: Chickenstuffer
desc: Start back in the 'cave' and climb through the obvious crack.
location: In 'cave' at the Chickenhawk area.

name: Shortcut
desc: Start same holds as Chickenhawk but using and undercling for a right. Dyno right and up to a slopey lip.
location: Chickenhawk boudler.

name: Ole Bull
desc: Stand start with right hand on a sloper and left hand on an undercling crack. Compress your way up to a jug top
location: Behind the Chickenhawk boulder if you're looking directly at the Chickenhawk line.

name: Chickenhawk
desc: Sit start matched on an obvious flat hold. do some funky beta working left and up onto the second block, either dyno or deadpoint to crimp. Hold the crux swing once you get your right hand up then top out with the jug crack. So good.
location: Right side of cave.

name: The Great Divide
desc: Climb through the obvious crack.
location: Crack on the right side of the Uptown Area behind DiSanto.

name: Swamp Thing
desc: Climb the small slab on the left side of the arete. Start both hands in vertical cracks
location: Left most line in the Uptown Area

name: Sidewinder
desc: Climb directly up on a unique crack
location: Left corner of easier climbs in Uptown Area

name: Trad Style
desc: Start in the right crack liebacking all the way up to the top. Crack gets a bit larger the further you go up.
location: Right crack on the left side of the Uptown area

name: The Vision
desc: Climb vertical face then go a bit left onto the slab. Starts left hand sidepull, right hand on a crimp.
location: left side of the uptown area

name: Spring Cleaning
desc: Stand start on the left arete with a pretty big foot. Go up and right climbing up slopers.
location: Face you first see when you enter Uptown Area

name: The Proud
desc: Climb up right side of the middle face using the arete for a right and a sidepull for your left. You can use the block below you for feet.
location: Left side of Uptown Area

name: The Mast
desc: Compression line. Stand start compressing the wide block. Smear and hug your way all the way up to the top.
location: Right most line of small grouping of climbs on the left side of the Uptown area

name: Bruno
desc: Stand start on a sideways jug. Snake your way right then left through a crack afterwards using crimps on the face.
location: There is a obvious low block on this one. Between the boulders that have DiSanto and The Mast on them

name: Sit & Grovel
desc: Sit start on obvious jug with a right heel. There's a sloper far left that you'll utilize for a mantle in the near future. Use the left arete and reach to jugs in the back.
location: Line to the right of Bruno

name: DiSanto Stand
desc: Stand start DiSanto on large sidepull and and incut crimp.
location: Right side of Uptown area

name: Yin Yang Arete
desc: Stand start anywhere on the arete with your right hand and left hand on an undercling crimp. Smear and dyno for the lip.
location: Right arete of boulder face that shares Sit & Grovel.

name: DiSanto
desc: Sit start with a cool crimpy pinch right hand and a sidepull for your left. Go big to sidepull and climb through afterwards using slopers to get to the lip.
location: Right side of Uptown Area.

name: Umbrella Configuration
desc: Start with left hand on jug and right on sloper. Work left and up to small dish and top out at the highest point on the left side.
location: Boulder you encounter before walking up to K-awareness area.

name: Trilogy
desc: Sit Start with right on the arete and left hand on a crimp rail. Do the diabase slap through slopers and top out.
location: 50 yards left of K-awareness.

name: Kinesthetic Awareness
desc: Start on flat rail all the way on the left side of the boulder at roughly head height. Do some cool beta working right until you reach the horn at the highest point in the cave, top out from there.
location: At the left side of the cave

name: Driven
desc: Stand Start on undercling, smear with left and throw a heel almost at head height with your right. Work up and left through slopers and top out utilizing the left protruding block.
location: To the right of K-Awareness

name: Kinesthetic Awareness Low
desc: Sit start directly under the massive sloper used on the stand with right hand in a square block and left on the lowest crimp. Pull off the ground and finish the same as the stand.
location: K-Awareness boulder

name: Mystere
desc: Navigate the arete up to the nose at the top
location: Visible from Trail 15 -- if you're approaching from the Ed Center, you'll see it on your left, and if you're approaching from PA-72, it will be on your right. Looks like a giant alligator about to eat something.

name: Who's Your Daddy
desc: Match the jug flake undercling under the huge roof. Fire to the lip and traverse right to a couple of good holds on the spine for the top out. Lower blocks are off.
location: Along the bouldering trail, towards the end, you'll see a large roof.
